text.p: Here is how major stock markets outside the United States ended on Monday.

LONDON - UK shares finished marginally lower on Monday, weighed down by a batch of ex-dividend stocks as well as uncertainty over forthcoming comment on financial markets from Fed chairman Alan Greenspan. Fears that the U.S. central bank chief could hint at higher interest rates or attempt to pour cold water on a hot stock market when he testifies before the U.S. Congress on Wednesday and Thursday, outweighed a firmer tone on Wall Street. The FTSE ended 5.7 points lower at 4,331.1.

FRANKFURT - German shares sliped to fresh losses in post-bourse IBIS electronic dealings, weighed on by losses on Wall Street and the dollar falling below 1.67 marks. Lack of fresh fundamental data keeps market interest limited and trading volumes relatively thin. In post-bourse trase the DAX stood at 3180.63 down 23.16.
Earlier the DAX ended bourse trade up 0.12 points at 3,184.21 points.
PARIS - French shares finished barely higher after trading in a 20-point range during the day.

Traders said the market was still consolidating but falls were limited by buying on the first day of the new account. Dollar weakness against the mark and softer bond markets also weighed on the market, which was otherwise livened by sharp rises in Club Med, CLF-Dexia and AGF.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 5.01 points or 0.2 percent at 2,567.85 while the CAC-40 futures contract was down at 2,570 from 2,577 on Friday's close.

ZURICH - Swiss shares continued Friday's consolidation, slipping below 4,500 points in the blue-chip Swiss Market Index (SMI) on profit taking. Activity picked up near the end of the session after Wall Street moved into positive terrain, but volumeswere low as insecurity about further developments prevailed.
The SMI ended down 59.3 points, or 1.13 percent, at 4,463.2 and the all-share Swiss Performance Index fell 34.24 points, or 1.19 percent, to 2,837.0.

TOKYO - Tokyo stocks sank on Monday as the momentum of buy-backs of bank and construction shares eased late in the session, eroding earlier gains. Profit-taking sales of blue-chip issues, which had appreciated in recent months, added to the losses. The Nikkei average of 225 leading shares ended at 18,896.99, down 137.55 points or 0.72 percent.

HONG KONG -Hong Kong's blue chips closed lower on Monday amid caution ahead of Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's Senate testimony this week and the political situation in Beijing, but China-related shares jumped.
The Hang Seng Index fell 69.16 points, or 0.51 percent, to 13,375.69. Turnover was HK$8.80 billion compared with HK$8.21 billion on Friday.

SYDNEY - Australian shares closed higher on Monday, the market carried to a firmer finish in light choppy trade by a modest rally staged in CRA and mild gains amongst most of the others. The All Ordinaries index gained 7.3 points to 2,482.6.

JOHANNESBURG - South African gold shares ended slightly firmer on Monday but profit-taking and a strong rand limited late gains. There was demand for industrial stock and further gains could be expected on the industrial board within the next one or two days provided the rand managed to sustain its firmer trend. The all-share index rose 28.2 points to new all-time closing high of 7,152.3 from its previous record closing high of 7,124.1 on Friday. The gold index was up 11.5 points to 1,529.3 and the industrial index gained 10.9 points to 8,390.2.
